title: Relative limit reduction to initial objects in disjoint components
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and relative limit diagrams and join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $I$ be a small set, possibly empty, and let $J=\coprod_{i\in I}J_i$ be the degreewise disjoint union of small quasicategories. Suppose each $J_i$ has an initial object $t_i$, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_{J_i}(t_i,z)$ is contractible for every $z\in J_i$. Let $I_{\mathrm{disc}}$ be the discrete simplicial set on $I$, and let $e:I_{\mathrm{disc}}\to J$ select the $t_i$. Let $p:D\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, $f:J\to D$ a functor and $g:J^{\triangleleft}\to B$ a cone satisfying $g|_J=pf$. There exists a $p$-limit diagram $q:J^{\triangleleft}\to D$ with $q|_J=f$ and $pq=g$ exactly if and only if there exists a $p$-limit diagram $q_0:I_{\mathrm{disc}}^{\triangleleft}\to D$ with $q_0|_{I_{\mathrm{disc}}}=fe$ and $pq_0=ge^{\triangleleft}$ exactly. Moreover, for any specified cone $q:J^{\triangleleft}\to D$, it is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if $qe^{\triangleleft}$ is one. The assertions include the empty indexing set and do not assume other limits in $D$.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.2.9 (02XT), existence under left-cofinal restriction, and Corollary 7.2.2.2 (02XQ), preservation and reflection of relative limits; the initial-object inclusions are left cofinal by the opposite of Corollary 4.7.3.22 (02J5), componentwise. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags. Read online; archive WANTED.

proof.text: For every $i$, apply the opposite and mapping-space clauses of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4). The simplicial set $J_i^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory, and $\operatorname{Map}_{J_i^{\mathrm{op}}}(z,t_i)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{J_i}(t_i,z)$ is weakly contractible by the hypothesis. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne] says that $r_i:\{t_i\}\hookrightarrow J_i^{\mathrm{op}}$ is right anodyne. This uses its final-vertex criterion on the opposite category, so the direction of the mapping spaces agrees with the initial-object hypothesis.

source.place: Corollary 4.7.3.22, final-vertex criterion applied to each opposite component.

proof.text: Put $A=I_{\mathrm{disc}}^{\mathrm{op}}=I_{\mathrm{disc}}$, $C=J^{\mathrm{op}}=\coprod_iJ_i^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $r=e^{\mathrm{op}}:A\hookrightarrow C$. Opposite commutes with this degreewise disjoint union, since it merely changes the simplicial operators. The map $r=\coprod_i r_i$ is right anodyne by the pushout and transfinite-composition closures of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]: well order the small set $I$; start with all the singleton summands, replace one singleton by its $J_i^{\mathrm{op}}$ at each successor stage, and take the degreewise union at each limit stage. Each successor map is a pushout of $r_i$, and the composite is exactly $r$. If $I=\varnothing$, it is the identity of the empty simplicial set, included in the defining class. In particular, $r$ is degreewise injective.

source.place: Componentwise extension using the weakly saturated definition of right anodyne maps.

proof.text: First prove the assertion for every specified cone $q$. By [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4), $q$ is a $p$-limit diagram exactly when $Q=q^{\mathrm{op}}:C^{\triangleright}\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-colimit diagram, and the same duality identifies the restricted cones. Write $x=Q(*)$ and $F=Q|_C$. For every vertex $z$ of $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] tests this colimit property on the square with left column $\operatorname{Map}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}(p(x),p(z))$ and right column $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,D^{\mathrm{op}})}(F,\Delta_Cz)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,B^{\mathrm{op}})}(p^{\mathrm{op}}F,\Delta_Cp(z))$. Restricting along $r$ leaves the left column unchanged. Both right-column restriction maps are equivalences by [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], applied to the right anodyne monomorphism $r$ and respectively to the quasicategories $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $B^{\mathrm{op}}$. The constant-test statement is natural in restriction, so the cone maps and their specified homotopies restrict to those of $Q r^{\triangleright}$.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.2, expanded using the existing anodyne restriction theorem, the constant-object test (02X1) and homotopy-pullback invariance (032B).

proof.text: To check the strict-span hypotheses of [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], denote the upper-right, lower-left and lower-right spaces by $U,V,W$, with maps $u:U\to W$ and $v:V\to W$, and put primes on the corresponding restricted spaces. Let $a:U\to U'$ and $c:W\to W'$ be restriction and $b=\mathrm{id}_V$. Choose the composition representatives and the cone homotopy in the constant test on $C$; use their restrictions for the test on $A$, as permitted by its naturality clause. Restriction of diagrams commutes with postcomposition by $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ degree by degree, giving $cu=u'a$, and restriction of the chosen base cocone gives $cv=v'b$. In each simplicial degree the resulting path-pullback map is $(h,k,\gamma)\mapsto(a(h),k,c\gamma)$; its endpoint equations are precisely these two equalities.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.2, expanded using the existing anodyne restriction theorem, the constant-object test (02X1) and homotopy-pullback invariance (032B).

proof.text: Thus [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] applies to these strictly commuting spans and makes this map a weak equivalence. The specified cone homotopy is restricted by the same rule, so it also identifies the comparison maps into the path pullbacks. The upper-left comparison maps have the same source and commute with this equivalence, so one is a weak equivalence exactly when the other is (on components and each homotopy group this is two-out-of-three for bijections and group isomorphisms). Hence the testing square is a homotopy pullback exactly when the restricted testing square is. This holds for every $z$, proving that $q$ is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if $qe^{\triangleleft}$ is.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.2, expanded using the existing anodyne restriction theorem, the constant-object test (02X1) and homotopy-pullback invariance (032B).

proof.text: Now suppose the required $q_0:I_{\mathrm{disc}}^{\triangleleft}\to D$ exists. Apply the pushout-join clause of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to $r:A\hookrightarrow C$ and the monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. It makes $N=(A\star\Delta^0)\amalg_A C\hookrightarrow C\star\Delta^0$ inner anodyne. Taking opposites and using the join identification of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4) gives $m:M=I_{\mathrm{disc}}^{\triangleleft}\amalg_{I_{\mathrm{disc}}}J\hookrightarrow J^{\triangleleft}$. This is still inner anodyne: reversal sends $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-k}^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, with $0<n-k<n$ when $0<k<n$; its involution also preserves pushouts, transfinite composites and retract diagrams.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.2.9, left-anodyne case, with the opposite of the pushout-join theorem 018J; explicit extension over the fixed base cone.

proof.text: Glue $q_0$ and $f$ on $M$; they agree exactly on $I_{\mathrm{disc}}$ because $q_0|_{I_{\mathrm{disc}}}=fe$. Their projection under $p$ is exactly $g|_M$, by the prescribed base equality for $q_0$ and $g|_J=pf$. The inner fibration definition [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies a filler for each inner horn, and therefore for $m$: lifting is preserved under pushout by extending on the attached summand and gluing; under transfinite composition by successive compatible fillers and the colimit map at limit stages; and under retracts by extending across the larger arrow and restricting by its section. Isomorphisms lift by their inverses. This is precisely the weakly saturated inner-anodyne class defined in the anodyne-cocone statement. We obtain $q:J^{\triangleleft}\to D$ extending the glued map over $g$. Thus $q|_J=f$, $pq=g$, and $qe^{\triangleleft}=q_0$ hold exactly, including the apex and all higher cone simplices. Step 5 makes $q$ a $p$-limit diagram.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.2.9, left-anodyne case, with the opposite of the pushout-join theorem 018J; explicit extension over the fixed base cone.

proof.text: Conversely, if a $p$-limit extension $q$ of $f$ over $g$ exists, put $q_0=qe^{\triangleleft}$. The equalities $q_0|_{I_{\mathrm{disc}}}=fe$ and $pq_0=ge^{\triangleleft}$ follow by composition, and Step 5 gives its $p$-limit property. Together with Steps 6–7 this proves both directions of the existence equivalence, as well as the already proved particular-cone clause. For $I=\varnothing$ both indexing simplicial sets are empty, $e$ is the identity, and both cones are the same point over the same vertex of $B$; the proof asserts the equivalence of the two identical existence problems, without asserting either has a solution. No other limit in $D$ has been assumed.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.2.9, forward implication; empty indexing set checked explicitly.
